name: Committees weighted the same evidence differently
justification: The set was empty. The committees did not see different facts; they weighted the same facts differently. R05 covers an issue that only one committee saw.

name: One committee's reviews were thin or inattentive
justification: The set was empty. B's short, uncritical reviews helped put its mean (7.75) above A's (7.0). This reason names review quality; R05 names a specific missed issue and R08 a rating that contradicts its own text.

name: Only one committee raised a substantive concern
justification: The set was empty. A alone questioned the core motivation and the closest competitor, and A's area chair kept both as required revisions. R06 covers issues that both committees saw.

name: Rebuttal moved one committee but not the other
justification: The set was empty. The response moved f6JJ's score and B's area chair called it 'particularly good', but no A score moved. R07 covers score changes that come from other reviewers, not from the response.

name: Area chair's own judgement drove the recommendation
justification: The set was empty. B's area chair, not B's reviewers, carried the oral. This reason names who decided; R02 names what a decision rested on, and a reviewer can also make that kind of claim.

name: One committee's reviewers left the rebuttal unanswered
justification: In A, oCAy never replied to a response that answered its ReActNet request and FCVA left no note, so pre-response scores stood while two B reviewers engaged and raised.

name: Reviewer's rating out of line with own text
justification: The set was empty. FCVA's 6 sits below its own positive text and lowered the mean that A's area chair leaned on. R04 does not fit: FCVA spent 10 hours, so the problem is the rating, not inattention.

name: Recommendation rested on a forecast of broad impact
justification: The set was empty. B's oral rests on a forecast of impact beyond BNNs, and the paper does not test that forecast. R01 covers an area chair who decides alone; this reason covers the content of the argument, from any member of a committee.

name: Reviewer discussion moved one committee's scores
justification: The set was empty. oG66 credited the other reviewers, not the authors, for the raise. R03 covers score changes that the response causes.

name: Committees weighted the same evidence differently
justification: Both committees saw dense notation and no experiments. A's area chair made 'very difficult to follow' the verdict, and Reviewer_yA7o held the missing experiments against the paper. B treated readability as fixable, and Reviewer_kvzq wrote 'I don't think that can be held against the work'.

name: One committee's reviews were thin or inattentive
justification: A's scores rest on less scrutiny. Reviewer_yA7o spent 2 hours, did not check the proofs, and its update names no gap; Reviewer_6Pv4 did not check the claims. A's reported hours average 4.0, B's 6.3.

name: Only one committee raised a substantive concern
justification: Only A's Reviewer_h23K said that Theorem 2's surrogate set turns the problem back into MGT. The paper confirms it, the response did not answer it, and it underlies h23K's 6. B's Reviewer_kvzq called the criteria 'a strict generalization'.

name: Higher tier given with no stated grounds
justification: B's oral exceeds its scores (top 8, 'Top 50% of accepted'). No reviewer asked for it, and the meta-review gives only 'a solid and novel theoretical contribution' as grounds.

name: Rebuttal moved one committee but not the other
justification: The response moved B's Reviewer_iUkv from 5 to 6 ('they have clarified my main concerns'), and B's area chair cited that raise. No A score moved; Reviewer_yA7o read the response and kept its concerns.

name: Area chair's own judgement drove the recommendation
justification: B's area chair chose an oral that no reviewer asked for. B's top score was 8 ('Top 50% of accepted NeurIPS papers'), and the meta-review gives only 'a solid and novel theoretical contribution' as grounds.

name: Rebuttal could answer one committee's concerns only
justification: B's main concern, notation, was answered in the response and moved iUkv from 5 to 6. A's main concerns (Theorem 2 depth, journal fit, the continuous case, missing experiments) could not be fixed in a response, and no A score moved.

name: Committees applied different standards for the contribution type
justification: A's yA7o required experiments of an identification-theory paper and held their absence against it. B's kvzq said a theory paper should not be penalised for that.

name: Unsure reviewers defaulted to a borderline score
justification: Three of A's four reviewers said they could not judge the paper and rated 6, and A's area chair took the flat 6s as the verdict. In B only Reviewer_iUkv said so; B's other reviewers rated 8 and 7. R04 does not cover this: Reviewer_rBKj spent 7 hours and read closely, so its 6 shows doubt, not inattention. R08 does not fit, because these reviews state no verdict for the 6 to contradict.

name: Audience or venue-fit objection lowered one committee
justification: A's 6Pv4 judged the paper better suited to a journal because its proofs need days to check, and stage 1 lists that among A's reasons for the poster. B raised no venue-fit point.

name: Committees weighted the same evidence differently
justification: Both committees saw the first coreset for decision trees, weak exposition and thin related work. B's area chair judged the novelty 'absolutely above the bar' and treated the writing as fixable in revision. A's area chair gave the same praised novelty a poster.

name: One committee's reviews were thin or inattentive
justification: B's only score above 7, Reviewer_1UMR's 8 at confidence 2, rests on a two-sentence main review that names no weakness and did not check the math. A's reviews also carry less scrutiny than B's other three: A averaged 3.0 hours against B's 4.0, and two A reviewers misstated the main bound as linear in k.

name: Only one committee raised a substantive concern
justification: Only B raised the gap between single-tree theory and the forest and boosting experiments, the uncited database-histogram work and the Algorithm 2 flaw. Reviewer_nDd9's 4 rests partly on the first two, and B's meta-review lists 'comparison to past work' among its 'very substantial concerns'. These concerns helped put B's mean below A's, though B's area chair still chose an oral.

name: Higher tier given with no stated grounds
justification: No B reviewer argued for an oral, B's mean is below A's, and B's meta-review calls the writing 'almost ... unpublishable'; nothing in the public record argues for the oral tier.

name: Area chair's own judgement drove the recommendation
justification: B's area chair chose an oral that no reviewer asked for. B's ratings (4, 7, 7, 8; mean 6.5) sit below A's poster ratings (mean 6.67). B's meta-review calls the writing 'almost of the level of being considered unpublishable', and its 'absolutely above the bar' appears in no public review or comment.

name: Non-expert reviewers' accept scores counted in full
justification: B's Reviewer_1UMR gave an 8 at confidence 2 without checking the math; it is B's only score above 7, and B's area chair drew on its praise for an oral that its checked reviews (4, 7, 7) did not support.

name: Damaging rebuttal admission did not lower scores
justification: The authors conceded to B that the theory is 'less clear' for the dependent trees of boosting used in the experiments; no B score fell and B's area chair still gave an oral.

name: Area chair relied on off-record reviewer input
justification: B's oral rests on 'absolutely above the bar', a judgement that appears in no public review or comment, used to set a tier that the visible reviews did not support.

name: Committees weighted the same evidence differently
justification: Both committees saw that the work builds on prior ideas: A's Reviewer_yauQ named C-learning, and B's Reviewer_6QWr called the rationale 'not necessarily novel'. A's area chair read the paper as 'a mix of existing and new tools'. In B, Reviewer_6QWr still called the work 'very high quality', and B's area chair named no weakness.

name: One committee's reviews were thin or inattentive
justification: B's top score came from a thin review. Reviewer_xycR's 9, the only 9 among the seven reviews, rests on a 2-hour, one-paragraph review with 'one minor comment'. Reviewer_LgSM's 8 rests on general praise and a raise that names no specific point. The careful reviews are close (A: 7, 7; B: 7, 8). A's one thin review, Reviewer_FCFz's, gave 8.

name: Only one committee raised a substantive concern
justification: Only A raised the simple image tasks and the claims with no linked experiment. Both points are correct, and the paper concedes the image limitation in Sec. 6. These doubts held A's Reviewer_3uQ8 at 7 after the rebuttal, while B's reviewers praised the experiments as 'comprehensive' and 'extensive'.

name: Rebuttal could answer one committee's concerns only
justification: B's concerns (halting, success-example actions, data needs) were questions the response answered, lifting Reviewer_9r4w to 8; A's concerns (simple image tasks, theory from C-learning, unlinked claims) no response could fix, and Reviewer_3uQ8 stayed at 7.

name: One outlying score set the tier
justification: Reviewer_xycR's 9, the outlying champion score from a one-paragraph review, lifted B's mean to 8.0, while B's remaining 8, 7, 8 are close to A's 7, 7, 8.

name: Reviewers placed similar verdicts at different scores
justification: Both committees wrote similar praise but scored it differently: B's generic reviews gave 9 and 8, Reviewer_6QWr's 'very high quality' gave 7, and B's area chair set the oral by the scores alone.

name: Committees weighted the same evidence differently
justification: Both committees saw the same complete criterion, dense notation and idealized experiments. A's area chair called clarity 'the main shortcoming of the paper'. B's area chair quoted Reviewer_rfa1's 'clear, rigorous, and well written' and named no weakness, though Reviewer_1SfX, Reviewer_4Bw1 and Reviewer_3m9X called the paper dense, hard to parse or abstract.

name: One committee's reviews were thin or inattentive
justification: B's only score above 7, Reviewer_rfa1's 9 at confidence 4, rests on three generic sentences ('clear, rigorous, and well written') and a list of presentation nits. It says nothing about the proofs, Algorithm 1 or the novelty over Zhang et al. (2020). Two more B reviewers rated 7 at confidence 1 without assessing the theory: Reviewer_nWYc knows 'very little about the technical details of causal learning', and Reviewer_4Bw1 gives no support for 'original and high quality'. Stage 1 finds no inattentive review in A.

name: Meta-review dropped the reviewers' stated weaknesses
justification: B's meta-review quotes Reviewer_rfa1 and Reviewer_3m9X and mentions no weakness, though its reviewers called the paper dense and the experiments artificial; A's meta-review kept 'the main shortcoming of the paper is its clarity'.

name: Higher tier given with no stated grounds
justification: B's meta-review only says 'It is my pleasure to recommend acceptance' and gives no reason for an oral over four 7s and one 9.

name: One outlying score set the tier
justification: Reviewer_rfa1's 9 against four 7s lifts B's mean from 7.0 to 7.4, and without it B's scores match A's mean of 7.0.

name: Area chair followed one outlying reviewer
justification: B's area chair gave an oral with no reason beyond two quotes, chiefly Reviewer_rfa1's 'clear, rigorous, and well written', and named none of the weaknesses that Reviewer_1SfX, Reviewer_4Bw1 and Reviewer_3m9X raised. Without rfa1's 9, B's mean equals A's 7.0. R01 does not fit: it needs the chair's own reading, and B's chair gave none; it passed on one reviewer's verdict. R04 covers how thin rfa1's review is, not the chair's choice to let one reviewer outweigh four. R06 covers how the two committees weighted clarity, not how one chair combined its own reviewers.

name: Committees weighted the same evidence differently
justification: Both committees questioned whether the model's fast transmission between rate units is biologically realistic. A's Reviewer_BSPV called it 'this major caveat to the biological plausibility of the model', then raised to 7 on a promised limitations section, and A's area chair did not mention it. B's area chair made 'the timescales of synaptic transmission' a required revision. This cause is secondary: the specific points B weighed came from VGyX alone (R05).

name: One committee's reviews were thin or inattentive
justification: A's scores rest on less scrutiny. A's top score, Reviewer_DcW4's 9, came after 2 hours with generic praise, no weakness or question, and the wrong claim that prospective coding 'has no precedence in the literature'. Reviewer_ob4X's 8 came after 2 hours in one paragraph. No A reviewer raised the prior work on fast population responses. B's 9 (Reviewer_iVNT) also admits confusion, but B's Reviewer_VGyX ran the code and checked the literature.

name: Only one committee raised a substantive concern
justification: Only B's Reviewer_VGyX showed that faster-than-τm responses were known and uncited (Knight 1972; van Vreeswijk and Sompolinsky 1998). He also showed that the noise filter uses synaptic time constants of 0.1 to 2 ms. The camera-ready concedes both points. His 3 rests on them, and B's area chair made both required revisions, suggested a new title and stopped at a poster. No A reviewer raised either point.

name: Meta-review dropped the reviewers' stated weaknesses
justification: A's one-sentence meta-review cites 'thorough experimental results' and omits BSPV's plausibility caveat, BSPV's 'a bit simplistic' robustness view and ztYa's requested comparisons; B's meta-review carried VGyX's points forward as required revisions.

name: Rebuttal moved one committee but not the other
justification: The response moved A's Reviewer_BSPV up to 7 ('Based on the authors' response, I have revised my score to an accept') on the promise of a limitations section. No B score moved: Reviewer_VGyX stayed 'still convinced' at 3, and Reviewer_gRxq and Reviewer_iVNT kept 8 and 9.

name: Score rested on a factual misreading of the paper
justification: A's Reviewer_DcW4 gave a 9 partly on the wrong claim that prospective coding 'has no precedence in the literature', which the paper's own Köndgen citation and Brea et al. 2016 contradict.

name: Rebuttal could answer one committee's concerns only
justification: A's main concerns (limitations section, Brea citation, wording of the forgetting claim) could be closed in the response and BSPV rose; B's main concern, that faster-than-τm responses were known and need short time constants, no response could fix, and no B score moved.

name: Non-expert reviewers' accept scores counted in full
justification: B's Reviewer_iVNT gave a 9 at confidence 4 while admitting 'uncertainties in my understanding' of Eq. 2 and Fig. 1, and B's area chair accepted on the 9 and the 8 at full weight.

name: Scores rose on unverified rebuttal evidence
justification: A's Reviewer_BSPV raised to 7 on a promised limitations section, and his follow-up question on whether rate coding brings back the lag got no technical answer.

name: Novelty judged against wrong or ignored prior work
justification: A's DcW4 accepted a 'no precedence' claim that the paper's own citations contradict, and no A reviewer knew the Knight and van Vreeswijk–Sompolinsky prior work on faster-than-τm responses that B's VGyX cited.

name: One outlying score set the tier
justification: VGyX's 3 against 9 and 8 pulled B's mean to 6.67; without him B's ratings (9, 8) exceed A's mean of 8.0.

name: Committees weighted the same evidence differently
justification: Both committees saw that the work extends Marteau-Ferey et al. with the same tools. A's Reviewer_rN14 called the gain 'somewhat incremental', and A's area chair made the comparison its only request. B's Reviewer_r7mh called the same fact a small issue and framed the result as the answer to an open question, which B's area chair repeated.

name: One committee's reviews were thin or inattentive
justification: B's higher mean rests partly on thin support. Reviewer_KRE1 gave 8 at confidence 5 with a six-sentence review of praise, no technical criticism and no sign of a math check, and it missed the qualification error. A's thin review (Reviewer_xAhK, 3 hours) gave only 7, in line with A's other reviewers.

name: Non-expert reviewers' accept scores counted in full
justification: B's Reviewer_r7mh rated 8 at confidence 2, and Reviewer_KRE1 rated 8 at confidence 5 with no sign of a math check; B's area chair counted both at full weight in the 7.75 mean that set the spotlight.

name: Authors told the two committees different things
justification: On Tikhonov's qualification the authors gave A a 'different notation' defence but conceded the error to B, so the two committees saw different accounts of the same point.

name: Reviewers placed similar verdicts at different scores
justification: Stage 1 calls the split 'score calibration, not substance'. R06 covers the one weighting difference (novelty), but most of the gap is reviewers on both sides giving the same verbal verdict different numbers, which no existing reason names. R08 is a single reviewer's text against their own rating, and here each rating fits its text.

name: Committees weighted the same evidence differently
justification: Both committees saw that the main experiments use only last-layer Laplace (A's Reviewer_z1y4, B's Reviewer_d2CF). B's area chair listed it as a remaining concern behind the poster; A's area chair did not mention it.

name: One committee's reviews were thin or inattentive
justification: A's record is thinner: about 10.5 reviewer-hours against B's 26, and Reviewer_aGgD gave 7 at confidence 1 after 1.5 hours and a 'cursory glance', praised the flawed Fig. 6, and still counted toward A's unanimous 7s.

name: Only one committee raised a substantive concern
justification: Only B found the undisclosed CIFAR-10-C loader bug behind Fig. 6 and pressed the DSCS-kernel motivation until the authors' ablation showed a quadratic kernel nearly matches it. B's area chair cited unresolved motivation for the poster, and B's two 6s stayed.

name: Meta-review dropped the reviewers' stated weaknesses
justification: A's two-sentence meta-review omits z1y4's 'somewhat limited' significance, h4G7's doubt on adoption and the last-layer-Laplace-only experiments; B's meta-review carried motivation and last-layer Laplace forward as remaining concerns.

name: Higher tier given with no stated grounds
justification: A's spotlight rests on a meta-review that gives no reason for the higher tier, and no A reviewer rated above 7 or argued for a spotlight.

name: Rebuttal could answer one committee's concerns only
justification: A's main concerns (missing baselines, approximation rigor) were closed by new numbers and promises, lifting three A reviewers to 7; B's DSCS-motivation and infinite-ReLU framing concern could not be answered and held Reviewer_4z2v at 6.

name: Non-expert reviewers' accept scores counted in full
justification: Reviewer_aGgD (confidence 1, 1.5 hours, 'cursory glance', proofs unread) gave 7, which counted in full toward the unanimity behind A's spotlight.

name: Damaging rebuttal admission did not lower scores
justification: B's authors admitted the CIFAR-10-C loader bug and that the rerun left RGPR barely above LLL, yet Reviewer_oTxs raised to 8 and Reviewer_YyKC to 6; no B score went down.

name: Scores rose on unverified rebuttal evidence
justification: R03 requires that the response leave the other committee unchanged, and here it moved both. The mechanism is the quality of the evidence behind A's raises, which turned A's mixed 6s and 7s into the unanimous 7s that preceded the spotlight; B's raises came only after a rerun.

name: Authors told the two committees different things
justification: Only B was told of the CIFAR-10-C loader bug, given the corrected rerun and shown the quadratic-kernel ablation; A judged the original Fig. 6 and received copied baseline numbers instead.

name: Unanimous scores read as grounds for higher tier
justification: R01 needs the area chair's own reading or taste, and A's meta-review gives none. R10 needs an outlying reviewer, and A had none. R11 is a calibration gap between similar verbal verdicts. None names agreement itself, rather than the level of the scores, setting the tier.

name: Committees weighted the same evidence differently
justification: Both committees saw the small robustness gain and the linearization gap; A's area chair named both as reservations behind the poster, while B's area chair named no weakness and wrote that the authors 'illustrated how to further boost adversarial robustness'.

name: One committee's reviews were thin or inattentive
justification: B's reviews were thin: Reviewer_HkhD gave the committee's top 7 after two hours with generic praise, Reviewer_aQh1 wrote two questions and a wrong limitation, and no B reviewer engaged after the rebuttal.

name: Only one committee raised a substantive concern
justification: Only A's Reviewer_7cFv showed that clean accuracy rises as much as AutoAttack accuracy (Table 3 confirms) and that pre-training plus retraining at least doubles cost; A's area chair carried 'the experimental results could be stronger' into the poster.

name: Meta-review dropped the reviewers' stated weaknesses
justification: R01 names the area chair's own taste setting the tier, and R06 names different weights on shared evidence. Neither names the area chair misreporting the committee's own record: B's meta-review omitted every weakness B's reviewers listed and contradicted Reviewer_aQh1's 'The robustness improvement is limited'. An area chair can do this while following the mean, so the mechanism is separate from R01.

name: Rebuttal moved one committee but not the other
justification: The response moved all three A reviewers up one point (mean 5.0 to 6.0), while no B reviewer replied to it or changed a score, so B's ratings stayed at their pre-rebuttal 6/7/6.

name: Area chair's own judgement drove the recommendation
justification: B's area chair gave a spotlight on their own reading ('a hot research topic', 'will interest many readers') although no B reviewer rated above 7 or asked for a highlight, so the tier sits above what B's 6/7/6 and arguments supported.

name: One committee's reviewers left the rebuttal unanswered
justification: No B reviewer replied to the 2021-08-10 responses (ClusTR comparison, wrong-hierarchy ablation, TRADES), so B's pre-rebuttal 6/7/6 stood, while all three A reviewers engaged and revised.

name: Recommendation rested on a forecast of broad impact
justification: B's spotlight rested on the area chair's forecast that the paper 'will interest many readers' in 'a hot research topic'; no reviewer on either committee made that forecast, and the paper's own gains are small.

name: Committees weighted the same evidence differently
justification: Both committees saw that Lemma 3.1 and the importance weighting are standard; B's Reviewer_dTZk listed them as pros and B's area chair praised the negative result, while A's Reviewer_i7rY counted them as known results without attribution.

name: One committee's reviews were thin or inattentive
justification: B's Reviewer_8ugy gave a thin 7 (generic praise, three questions, posted late, no reply to the rebuttal), and B's reviewers averaged 4.4 hours against A's 6.0.

name: Only one committee raised a substantive concern
justification: Only A's reviewers found the undefined fairness link, the incomplete and mis-cited related work, and the uncited standard tools, all confirmed by author concession or the camera-ready text; A's area chair called these 'major presentation concerns' and stopped at poster.

name: Rebuttal moved one committee but not the other
justification: The response moved A's Reviewer_oRvo (5 to 6) and Reviewer_i7rY up to 7, while no B score moved; here the asymmetry narrowed the gap rather than widened it.

name: Area chair's own judgement drove the recommendation
justification: No B reviewer rated above 7 or argued for a highlight, yet B's area chair gave a spotlight on its own reading ('a very strong contribution', 'I found the assumption ... odd'), one tier above what B's 7, 6, 7, 7, 7 supported.

name: Unanimous scores read as grounds for higher tier
justification: B's meta-review cited 'The reviewers were uniformly positive' among its grounds for a spotlight although no B reviewer rated above 7, while A's 6, 6, 7, 7 had the same maximum and a similar mean and got a poster.

name: Recommendation rested on a forecast of broad impact
justification: B's meta-review said the paper 'should be of interest not only to researchers in online learning but also the broader community'; no reviewer on either committee made that forecast, and A's area chair did not.

name: One committee's reviews were thin or inattentive
justification: A's three 8s include two thin reviews: Reviewer_PMym (two-sentence review, 2 hours, math not checked) and Reviewer_vxWe (no weakness named, confidence 3), against B reviews of 12 and 20 hours.

name: Only one committee raised a substantive concern
justification: Only B found the impossible min-max assumption, the 'complements, rather than improves' concession, the hidden log factor, the kappa^4 inner loop against STABLE and the eq. (48) error; B's area chair made the kappa comparison a requirement.

name: Meta-review dropped the reviewers' stated weaknesses
justification: A's three-sentence meta-review omitted Reviewer_TdaR's novelty doubt ('merely' Lemma 2) and the missing conclusion and called the analysis 'tight', while B's meta-review carried Reviewer_wdT9's kappa request forward as a requirement.

name: Rebuttal moved one committee but not the other
justification: The response moved B's Reviewer_b2gP up ('I have updated my score') after correcting its compositional misreading, while no A reviewer recorded a score change; here the asymmetry narrowed the gap.

name: Score rested on a factual misreading of the paper
justification: R04 covers thin or inattentive reviews, not a wrong statement about the paper's results; here a wrong claim in favour of the paper (PMym's overstated gain, the AC's 'tight') fed A's 8 and spotlight, and two wrong claims against it (b2gP's quadratic-only reading, wdT9's two-loop reading) fed B's early objections.

name: Non-expert reviewers' accept scores counted in full
justification: A's Reviewer_PMym and Reviewer_vxWe gave 8s at confidence 3 with 'math not carefully checked', and A's area chair counted them in full as 'consensus', which lifted A's mean to 7.75 and the spotlight.

name: Novelty judged against wrong or ignored prior work
justification: A's Reviewer_PMym accepted an improvement claim over 'previous work' that stocBiO and STABLE, already at O(eps^-2), contradict, and that verdict fed its 8.

name: Committees weighted the same evidence differently
justification: Both committees saw the same novel latent grammar, respectable small-scale results and expensive dynamic program; A's AC called the results 'strong' and downplayed scale, B's AC called them 'good'.

name: One committee's reviews were thin or inattentive
justification: A's champion Reviewer_e5Ff wrote a 9 in 2 hours with general praise, no question and one weakness that restates the paper's limitation, and that thin review lifted A's mean to 7.5.

name: Only one committee raised a substantive concern
justification: Only B raised the open positioning against NQG-T5 and the per-dataset tuned nonterminal counts and rule constraints; these held Reviewer_9RED and Reviewer_sHgm at 6 and B at poster.

name: Meta-review dropped the reviewers' stated weaknesses
justification: A's meta-review names high time complexity as 'the only main weakness' and calls the results 'strong', dropping Reviewer_FyUp's and Reviewer_fSHR's weak-MT-baseline concern and the authors' concession that a Transformer wins by 3 to 4 BLEU.

name: Score rested on a factual misreading of the paper
justification: A's Reviewer_e5Ff claimed the model beats seq2seq 'substantially' on MT and shows 'better sample efficiency', but the base model trails the LSTM (23.5 vs 25.1 BLEU) and no experiment varies data size; that error fed the 9 and the AC's 'strong'.

name: Non-expert reviewers' accept scores counted in full
justification: B's most specific reviewer, Reviewer_3r7i (8, confidence 4, engaged after the rebuttal), is neither cited nor weighed in B's meta-review, which follows the 6.75 mean to a poster.

name: Damaging rebuttal admission did not lower scores
justification: R03 covers a response that persuaded one committee and not the other, and R13 covers scores raised on unverified favourable evidence; neither covers a committee that received an unfavourable admission and did not act on it. R14 covers only the meta-review's omission, not the reviewers' failure to lower their scores.

name: One committee's reviewers left the rebuttal unanswered
justification: A's outlying Reviewer_e5Ff posted nothing after the rebuttal, which disclosed that a Transformer beats the model on MT, the claim behind its 9, so the 9 stood unrevised.

name: Authors told the two committees different things
justification: The authors conceded the Transformer's 3 to 4 BLEU lead only to A and gave the favourable pipelined and no-constraint tables only to B, so each committee judged different evidence.

name: One outlying score set the tier
justification: A's outlying 9 from Reviewer_e5Ff lifted A's mean from 7.0 to 7.5 and carried the spotlight, while A's other scores (7, 7, 7) match B's (6, 8, 7, 6) closely.

name: Area chair followed one outlying reviewer
justification: A's meta-review paraphrases the outlying 9 of Reviewer_e5Ff in structure and wording ('strong results', sample efficiency, time complexity as the only weakness) and sets aside the Transformer concern of the 7s.

name: Committees weighted the same evidence differently
justification: Both committees saw that the theory leans on Balcer and Vadhan [3]; A's Reviewer_WJWj counted it against the paper as incremental, while B's Reviewer_4cAR and Reviewer_eGa2 accepted the authors' answer and kept or raised their scores.

name: One committee's reviews were thin or inattentive
justification: B's 8 from Reviewer_bo89 is mostly a restated summary with no weakness named, and A's Reviewer_WJWj gave a 5 after 2 hours, asking a tightness question Theorem 4 answers and never replying to the authors.

name: Only one committee raised a substantive concern
justification: Only A raised mechanism specificity, tightness and writing quality; the two 5s rest on them, and A's meta-review carried the mechanism-specificity doubt forward as a reason for its divided view.

name: Meta-review dropped the reviewers' stated weaknesses
justification: B's meta-review restates the result and names no weakness its reviewers raised (reliance on [3], restriction to one error metric, overreaching microdata advice), while A's meta-review carries its reviewers' doubts forward.

name: Higher tier given with no stated grounds
justification: B's area chair chose a spotlight on 8, 7, 6, 6, two of them 'marginally above' and the 8 thinly argued, and the meta-review gives no reason for that tier.

name: Score rested on a factual misreading of the paper
justification: A's Reviewer_ecPK cut 6 to 5 on the wrong claim that subsampling amplification lets point queries take less noise so the trade-off fits one mechanism, and A's area chair repeated it; Reviewer_WJWj's tightness doubt is also contradicted by Theorem 4.

name: Area chair's own judgement drove the recommendation
justification: A's area chair accepted a 5, 7, 6, 5 panel on 'high significance and potential impact' against two below-threshold scores, and B's area chair chose a spotlight on 8, 7, 6, 6 from their own reading with no reason given for the tier.

name: Damaging rebuttal admission did not lower scores
justification: The authors told B that Theorem 3's novelty lies 'not in the proof' but in its interpretation, building on [3]'s Theorem 7.2, yet Reviewer_4cAR kept 7 and B's area chair gave a spotlight.

name: Late objection left the authors no reply
justification: R15 covers a wrong claim feeding a score, but not its timing; the cause here is that the objection came after the response closed, so the authors could not refute it as they did B's wrong objection. R03 covers a response that persuaded one committee, not an objection the response never saw.

name: Committees weighted the same evidence differently

name: Higher tier given with no stated grounds

name: Rebuttal could answer one committee's concerns only
justification: A's concerns were clarity gaps the authors closed with formal statements and Gumbel-max settings; B's main concern was the premise itself, which the authors conceded and no response could fix.

name: Non-expert reviewers' accept scores counted in full
justification: A's Reviewer_g3MG ('a bit beyond my expertise') and Reviewer_cSRr ('unable to assess the soundness') gave 7 at confidence 3 and 2, and the AC counted them at full weight.

name: Scores rose on unverified rebuttal evidence
justification: A's three reviewers raised to 7 on clarifications and promised camera-ready changes (a promised Gumbel-max derivation, an extra-page rewrite); none re-examined proofs or experiments.

name: One committee's reviewers left the rebuttal unanswered
justification: Reviewer_ybLo (3, B) and Reviewer_eGhr (5, A) never replied to the authors' answers; ybLo's 3 stood unrevised and the B AC adopted its stance.

name: Authors told the two committees different things
justification: On latent confounding A was told 'the same set of cases' as Oberst & Sontag and B 'Markovian models'; the 'cannot be falsified' concession went to B only.

name: Reviewer's rating out of line with own text
justification: Reviewer_eGhr's text praises the theory ('I haven't seen any other papers like it') and lists only minor clarity points, yet the rating is 5.

name: Committees weighted the same evidence differently
justification: Both committees saw the same Fig. 3 results, with Glove ahead on three of six graphs; A called it no clear superiority, B accepted 'the best or nearly the best'.

name: Only one committee raised a substantive concern
justification: Only A raised the uncited degree-debiasing literature (APPR, Lasagne, Fairwalk, role2vec, DEMO-Net), and A's meta-review lists novelty and missing comparisons as reasons to reject.

name: Meta-review dropped the reviewers' stated weaknesses
justification: B's meta-review called the concerns 'mostly regarding the presentation', which drops RJD5's train-test leak fix and the offset-only result at 96% of r2v's AUC.

name: Higher tier given with no stated grounds
justification: B's spotlight on 6, 6, 8, 7 has no stated grounds in the meta-review, and no reviewer argued for a highlight.

name: Rebuttal moved one committee but not the other

name: Score rested on a factual misreading of the paper
justification: A's Reviewer_2mkY wrongly said Glove is 'consistently performing better', and B's champion yRQF wrongly said r2v 'works empirically the best'; each claim fed that reviewer's score.

name: Non-expert reviewers' accept scores counted in full
justification: B's Reviewer_yRQF said it would 'rely on other reviewers to judge the originality' yet rated 8, and B's AC counted it in the mean behind the spotlight.

name: Damaging rebuttal admission did not lower scores
justification: B heard the authors concede that the degree offset alone reaches 96% of r2v's AUC and that node2vec beats r2v-dcSBM on impact factor after the leak fix, yet RJD5 raised from 4 to 6.

name: Committees applied different standards for the contribution type
justification: A judged the paper by state-of-the-art performance, which the authors asked q94Z not to use, while B accepted that understanding the degree bias, not accuracy, is the contribution.

name: One committee's reviewers left the rebuttal unanswered
justification: No A reviewer answered the 11 August replies, while B's RJD5 and yRN6 engaged over two rounds and raised.

name: Reviewer's rating out of line with own text
justification: A's Reviewer_MjL3 wrote only praise with no weakness or question yet rated 6, the borderline accept level.

name: Committees weighted the same evidence differently
justification: Both committees saw that guarantees hold only for correct predictions and robustness comes from the one-sentence γ-split; A's two confidence-4 reviewers rated 4 on it, while B's PbZr called robustness trivial and YbwL made it a revision item.

name: Only one committee raised a substantive concern
justification: Only A asked for a prediction-aware baseline and a closed-form ratio; A's meta-review counted the limited experiments against the paper, and no B reviewer questioned the ZCL-only design.

name: Higher tier given with no stated grounds
justification: B's three-sentence meta-review gives no reason for a spotlight over a poster with two 6s at confidence 4.

name: Rebuttal moved one committee but not the other
justification: The 2021-09-03 thread cleared YbwL's additive-loss misreading and YbwL raised to 6 in B, while A got the same (1+ε) sketch and nobody moved.

name: Score rested on a factual misreading of the paper
justification: A's K1Av said robustness is not discussed, though lines 87-89 state a worst-case bound, and A's xbrn offered a boundary counterexample outside the continuous model; both fed A's 4s.

name: Rebuttal could answer one committee's concerns only
justification: B's main open concern was a misreading the authors could clear by clarification, while A's concerns (robustness trade-off, framing, prediction-aware baseline) needed new results that no response could supply.

name: Non-expert reviewers' accept scores counted in full
justification: B's 8 (PbZr) and 7 (et4L) came at confidence 3 with math not carefully checked, while the two confidence-4 reviewers gave 6; the AC counted all four in full and reached a spotlight.

name: Committees applied different standards for the contribution type
justification: A held the paper to the consistency-robustness standard of learning-augmented algorithms and counted the missing trade-off against it, while B valued interval-prediction consistency on its own terms and called robustness trivial.

name: One committee's reviewers left the rebuttal unanswered
justification: No A reviewer posted or edited after the rebuttal, so the (1+ε) sketch and the γ-split pointer went unanswered, while B's YbwL and PbZr engaged and YbwL revised.

name: Committees weighted the same evidence differently

name: One committee's reviews were thin or inattentive
justification: A's only 8 came from Reviewer_88jd after one hour, in four short paragraphs, with an incorrect 'thoroughly tested' claim and no reply to the rebuttal.

name: Only one committee raised a substantive concern
justification: Only B raised that the full DBE trails its deterministic part DisAE+VAME, that interpretability is unproven, and that results rest on one dataset with single runs; these drove B's rejection.

name: Meta-review dropped the reviewers' stated weaknesses
justification: A's meta-review names no weakness, though its reviewers named missing ablations, poor generated videos, a code bug and clarity faults.

name: Higher tier given with no stated grounds
justification: A's spotlight rests on a generic meta-review ('a very good piece of work') with no argument for the tier.

name: Committees applied different standards for the contribution type
justification: A judged the paper as a neuroscience tool that beats baselines; B judged it as a methods paper and required the new stochastic model to add something, which it does not.

justification: Only B received new experiments ([31] baseline, view ablations, context results) and the authors' concession that they were 'perhaps overclaiming the interpretability'; A got neither.

name: Promised fixes judged too large without re-review
justification: B's AC judged the reframing 'as a study of different representations' too significant for a camera-ready, while A treated its issues as camera-ready fixes.

justification: Both committees saw the same simple loss, the same requests (ImageNet-1K, ResNet, longer training, lambda) and the same rebuttal answers; A's reviewers stayed below threshold and B's called the answers adequate.

name: One committee's reviews were thin or inattentive
justification: B's Reviewer_G9ps gave a 6 after three hours, misdescribed the setting as fine-tuning, named one weakness and answered the rebuttal with thanks only, while A's reviewers probed the evidence harder.

justification: B's meta-review named no remaining weakness and said the scale and CNN questions were addressed, dropping Z3Px's insufficiency verdict, K16j's 'high uncertainty' and its view that the optimization is 'likely poor throughout'.

justification: B gave a spotlight on ratings 6, 6, 5, 6 (mean 5.75) under a meta-review that gives no reason for the tier.

None covers a score held on a point that does not bear on the contribution.

justification: Only A's rPEM judged the Something-Something margins small and the rebuttal's Kinetics baselines weak, and A's AC adopted that list in the reject.

name: Meta-review dropped the reviewers' stated weaknesses
justification: B's three-sentence meta-review names no weakness, not even L4t3's 'a bit incremental and convoluted', while A's meta-review carried its reviewers' reservations forward.

name: Higher tier given with no stated grounds
justification: B's spotlight rests on no rating above 7 and a meta-review that names no strength or argument for that tier.

name: Rebuttal moved one committee but not the other
justification: B's Reviewer_1j5f moved toward acceptance after the rebuttal met its main concern (non-local baseline); no A score moved.

justification: B's main concerns (non-local baseline, parameter counts) were closable by new results, and 1j5f rose; A's decisive concerns (writing, incrementality) no rebuttal table could fix.

justification: rPEM posted 'not that significant' and 'kind of incremental' on 2021-08-29, after the rebuttal, with no author reply in the record, and A's AC adopted them; B's objections came before the rebuttal and were answered.

justification: A's DqnY raised to 6 'based on the assumption that the missing information will be added', on promised appendices and a code link, not checked evidence.

justification: B's Reviewer_DeZu cut 7 to 6 citing 'the weaknesses in the experiments section as other reviewers have noted', not the authors' response.

justification: B's final positions split 3 and 5 against 6 and 7 at confidence 3 to 4, and the AC settled it on xSwS's critique without addressing the accept-side scores; A had no split.

justification: A's Reviewer_Fjfm gave 9 ('Top 15% of accepted papers') while the text concedes 'Most of the ideas in this paper are not brand new' and ends 'I think it is a good paper', a 7-level verdict.

justification: B's two-sentence meta-review omits oWmh's and 9b2J's presentation complaints and the disclosed theorem error; A's calls all its reviewers' concerns 'minor comments'.

justification: A's spotlight sits above three 'marginally above threshold' ratings, and neither its reviews nor its meta-review give a reason for that tier.

justification: A's Q5eH said the paper studies infinite-width networks and ab3Y said it bounds random-features models, both wrong, and these readings underpinned their 6s and ab3Y's view that the results are mostly re-proofs.

name: Meta-review dropped the reviewers' stated weaknesses
justification: B's three-sentence meta-review drops iqKa's SoS caveat (only quotation marks around 'matches' remain), while A's meta-review carries 9Tob's caveat forward as a formal-proof request; the tier did not change.

name: Rebuttal moved one committee but not the other
justification: The authors' prior-work reply moved A's Reviewer_A5qv up to 7, while no B score moved; this only narrowed A's spread and changed no tier.

name: Novelty judged against wrong or ignored prior work
justification: A's Reviewer_A5qv first judged the conceptual gain limited because a d^2 bound 'follows from DKS17'; the paper credits that bound to DKS19, which needs an unknown covariance and does not transfer. The error held A5qv's first score down until the rebuttal corrected it.
